title: Gender, Race, and Intersectional Bias in Resume Screening via Language Model Retrieval
abstract: arXiv:2407.20371v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) hiring tools have revolutionized resume screening, and large language models (LLMs) have the potential to do the same. However, given the biases which are embedded within LLMs, it is unclear whether they can be used in this scenario without disadvantaging groups based on their protected attributes. In this work, we investigate the possibilities of using LLMs in a resume screening setting via a document retrieval framework that simulates job candidate selection. Using that framework, we then perform a resume audit study to determine whether a selection of Massive Text Embedding (MTE) models are biased in resume screening scenarios. We simulate this for nine occupations, using a collection of over 500 publicly available resumes and 500 job descriptions. We find that the MTEs are biased, significantly favoring White-associated names in 85.1\% of cases and female-associated names in only 11.1\% of cases

translated_title: 基于语言模型检索的简历筛选中的性别、种族及交叉性偏见
translated_abstract: 人工智能（AI）招聘工具已经彻底改变了简历筛选方式，而大型语言模型（LLM）也有潜力实现同样的变革。然而，鉴于LLM中嵌入的偏见，目前尚不清楚在这种场景中使用它们是否会对基于受保护属性的人群造成不利影响。在这项工作中，我们通过一个模拟职位候选人筛选的文档检索框架，研究了在简历筛选场景中使用LLM的可能性。利用该框架，我们随后进行了一项简历审计研究，以确定一系列大规模文本嵌入（MTE）模型在简历筛选场景中是否存在偏见。我们使用超过500份公开可用的简历和500份职位描述，对九种职业进行了模拟。我们发现MTE模型存在偏见，在85.1%的情况下显著偏好与白人相关的名字，而在仅有11.1%的情况下偏好与女性相关的名字。
tldr: 该研究通过模拟候选人筛选的文档检索框架对大规模文本嵌入模型进行简历审计，发现这些模型在简历筛选中存在显著偏见，在85.1%的情况下偏好白人相关名字，而仅在11.1%的情况下偏好女性相关名字。
en_tdlr: This study performs a resume audit of Massive Text Embedding models via a document retrieval framework simulating candidate selection, revealing significant biases that favor White-associated names in 85.1% of cases and female-associated names in only 11.1% of cases.
